threads.body:
Worth expanding this comment, because the call has a side effect that is not obvious from the
name: `LazyStorage.<clinit>` ends with `ContextStorageWrappers.setStorageInitialized()`, after
which every `ContextStorage.addWrapper(...)` call is dropped (logged only at `FINE`).

`runAfterAgentListeners(...)` runs ~15 lines below this, so any distro/extension that registers a
context storage wrapper from `AgentListener.afterAgent()` will now silently stop working. That is
probably an acceptable trade-off, but it should be spelled out here (and ideally in the PR
description).

Also worth restating the *why*: on 1.64.0 `LazyStorage.createStorage()` uses
`ComponentLoader.forClassLoader(LazyStorage.class.getClassLoader())`, so provider discovery no
longer walks the application class path the way the stack trace in
open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java#8434 shows. The hazard that remains (and that this fixes) is the
class-initialization monitor of `LazyStorage` being held by a thread that needs a class loader /
jar lock held by another thread that is itself waiting on that monitor.

```suggestion
    // eagerly initialize context storage before any instrumentation is active, so that its lazy
    // initialization cannot happen while an instrumented method holds a class loader lock that
    // the initializing thread needs, see
    // https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java/issues/8434
    // note that this also finalizes the storage - ContextStorage.addWrapper() calls made after
    // this point are ignored
```

replies.body: Expanded the comment to clarify the rationale and document the side effect
Removed the redundant context storage initialization

threads.body:
Is there a reason you chose to place this here instead of for example next to
https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/blob/0ae4cc70d2c2a2bd02f71a33f90b80db7e65ef99/javaagent-tooling/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/tooling/AgentInstaller.java#L117
I'm not opposed to this, but to me this looks more like an issue in the custom instrumentation than in the agent. Generally instrumentation authors need to take care when instrumenting code that runs early during the jvm start. I'd guess it could also be worked around by calling `Context.current()` in the constructor of their `InstrumentationModule` constructor.

replies.body:
I put it right before `installOn()` because `ContextStorage.get()` also finalizes the storage, so any later addWrapper() calls are ignored. Putting it near `preloadClasses()` would finalize it earlier than needed, before extensions are loaded and configured

Calling `Context.current()` from that particular InstrumentationModule would work as a workaround. My concern is that the same issue could happen with other instrumentations that touch context during early class loading, so initializing it just before the main transformer is installed seemed like a safer boundary
